name: Alexander Hamilton
role: First U.S. Secretary of the Treasury (1789-1795) and Federalist leader
summary: Hamilton argued for a strong national government with an energetic executive, an independent judiciary and a Senate and executive serving long terms. As Treasury Secretary he funded the national debt, founded a national bank on implied powers, and urged protective duties and bounties for manufactures. He opposed slavery, helped found the New York Manumission Society and welcomed immigration, while distrusting democratic excess and favoring British-style stability.
